message.reasoning: Okay, so I need to figure out whether deleting my step brother's profile on my Nintendo Switch is morally acceptable. Let me start by understanding the situation better. First, I had to watch my step brother for a week while my dad and his mom were on a trip. I brought my Switch because I wanted something to do during my long commute to school. My step brother really liked playing on it, so I created a new profile for him to keep his games separate from mine. That worked well because it helped distract him while I studied. But then, when I got back to school, I got annoyed every time I had to switch profiles to play my games or go to the eShop. So, I decided to delete his profile to make things easier for myself. Now, during Thanksgiving, my step brother found out his Zelda save was gone and he started crying. My dad thinks it was mean of me to delete it because he knew my step brother was enjoying playing on it. Hmm, so I need to evaluate if deleting his profile was morally acceptable. Let me think about the different aspects involved here. First, ownership. The Nintendo Switch is mine, right? So, I have the right to decide who uses it and how. I created a profile for him to use, but I also have the right to delete it if I want. But does that mean I can just delete it without considering his feelings? Then there's the issue of consent. I created the profile for him, but did I ever tell him that I might delete it in the future? Probably not. So, he had no idea that his profile could be deleted, and now he's upset because he lost his progress in Zelda. Another point is the impact of my action. My step brother was really enjoying playing on the Switch, and losing his save made him cry. That's a strong emotional reaction, which shows that my action had a negative impact on him. Also, my dad thinks it was mean. That suggests that from an external perspective, my action was not kind or considerate. It shows a lack of empathy towards my step brother's feelings. On the other hand, I was annoyed by having to switch profiles every time. It was inconvenient for me, and I wanted to make things easier. But is it worth causing someone else distress just for my convenience? I guess I need to weigh the importance of my convenience against the emotional impact on my step brother. It seems like my action caused more harm than good. Additionally, communication is key. If I was annoyed, maybe I could have talked to my step brother about it instead of just deleting his profile. That way, we could have found a solution together, like setting up a different profile or finding another way for him to play without affecting my games. So, in the end, deleting his profile without telling him or considering his feelings was not a morally acceptable action. It showed a lack of empathy and consideration for someone else's feelings, even though I had the right to manage my own property.
